mechanism: Constant positive std_range has zero log-range width. Explicit init_std divided by that width and wrote NaN biases, though the no-init_std path already supports constant ranges. Use a finite neutral raw bias for zero-width ranges; preserve the original inverse mapping otherwise.

pull_request.title: Handle fixed squashed-Gaussian deviation initialization
pull_request.body:
A fixed positive standard-deviation range already works for `SquashedGaussianDistribution` when `init_std` is omitted. Setting `std_range=(0.5, 0.5)` together with the matching `init_std=0.5` instead divides by the zero log-range width while initializing the output head. This writes NaN biases and produces NaN actions and SAC losses.

Use a finite neutral raw std-head bias when the range has zero width. Every finite raw head value maps to the same configured deviation in this case. Nonconstant ranges continue to use the existing inverse mapping.

The existing initialization regression now includes a constant range. A real SAC regression covers the same configuration with and without explicit initialization, checks finite losses and parameters after replay collection and an optimizer update, verifies that the deviation stays at 0.5, and confirms that the action mean still learns.

Validation on base `8945bdcbc364f388e14caebf547dbf302d89e491`, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.7.1+cpu and TensorDict 0.7.2:

- Unchanged source: 2 regression failures and 3 passing controls; corrected source: all 5 pass.
- Complete CPU suite: 290 passed, 6 CUDA-only cases skipped, including Gloo and JIT/ONNX tests.
- All configured pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

Both fixed-range SAC configurations now produce the same finite actor, critic and temperature losses under the same random seed. GPU and long-run convergence were not evaluated.

Validation: https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43674703143
